body:
In the MRP, `int("t1ex2t")` prints `12` and `print(float("t1ex2t"))` prints `0.0`. This works as documented, so it's not really undefined behaviour (although arguably a bit unintuitive). The string constructors are documented as following the same rules as `String.to_int()` and `String.to_float()`, which in turn say:

> Converts the string representing an integer number into an [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html#class-int). This method removes any non-number character and stops at the first decimal point (.).

> Converts the string representing a decimal number into a [float](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_float.html#class-float). This method stops on the first non-number character, except the first decimal point (.) and the exponent letter (e). See also [is_valid_float()](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_string.html#class-string-method-is-valid-float).

The docs even give an example that a string with no digits like "Hello" will return `0.0`, just like `float("t1ex2t")` does. The 3.6 docs are a bit less detailed, but still say something similar (including "Calling this method with an invalid float string will return 0").

If we want to change this behaviour or introduce some warning, then perhaps that would be more appropriate as a proposal than a bug report? @AThousandShips
Indeed, please suggest any changes in a [proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals)
